overview: The Mystic Valley Voter Forum hosted a candidate debate for the second Middlesex State Senate district, featuring four candidates who discussed affordability, racial disparity, international divestment, immigration, digital security, and accessibility.

items.title: Opening and Sponsoring Introductions
items.summary: Organizers welcomed attendees to the first Mystic Valley Voters Forum, sponsored by local civic, advocacy, and human rights organizations.

items.title: Candidate Introductions
items.summary: Candidates Erika Uyterhoeven, Burhan Azim, Matt McLaughlin, and Christine Barber introduced themselves and outlined their backgrounds and campaigns.

items.title: Affordability
items.summary: The candidates discussed housing production, utility costs, childcare affordability, and the impact of the MBTA Communities Act.

items.title: Racial Disparity
items.summary: Candidates addressed systemic racism and financial inequality, debating state-level solutions to healthcare access, wealth gaps, and criminal justice disparities.

items.title: Palestine and Local Policies
items.summary: The panel debated whether Israel's military actions in Gaza constitute genocide and discussed local and state pension fund divestment ordinances.

items.title: Immigration
items.summary: The candidates outlined their records and proposed state policies to safeguard immigrant communities from federal enforcement and deportations.

items.title: Digital Security
items.summary: Candidates discussed artificial intelligence regulations, data privacy legislation, social media restrictions, and state cybersecurity funding.

items.title: Closing Statements
items.summary: Each candidate presented a final summary of their political philosophy and vision for representation at the State House.

items.title: Public Q&A
items.summary: Candidates answered audience questions about municipal divestment rights, senior healthcare, public safety, and services for people with disabilities.

subject: Second Middlesex State Senate Candidate Debate
